I’m Yubo Jia, a Master’s student in Hydrology & Water Resources Engineering at Northwest A&F University (NWAFU) in Yangling, Shaanxi. I also completed my B.Eng. at NWAFU. Originally from Yulin, Shaanxi, China, I expect to graduate in 2026 and plan to pursue a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Technology at Northwestern Polytechnical University (NPU) in Xi’an.


My research centers on the AI–hydrology intersection, especially time-series modeling for rainfall–runoff and groundwater, physics-guided deep learning, and uncertainty quantification for decision-ready hydrologic forecasting and water resources management.



Build generalizable sequence models that learn across many basins while retaining local behavior.


Embed physical constraints and process cues into neural networks to improve robustness and interpretability.


Deliver calibrated prediction intervals and risk-aware metrics to support operations.



I value open science and reproducibility—notes and code are shared on GitHub, and I’m always glad to collaborate across hydrology, computer science, and applied-statistics communities.

title: Publications
text:
Journal Articles

Jia, Y. B., Su, X. L., Zhang, T., Wu, H. J., Jia, Y. Y., & Wang, Q. Y. (2025). Enhancing Streamflow Forecasting Using an LSTM Hybrid Model with Lightweight Frequency-Domain Feature Learning. Expert Systems with Applications. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2025.129418
Affiliations: Northwest A&F University (NWAFU); China Three Gorges University (CTGU); Northwestern Polytechnical University (NPU). Contribution: Proposed a lightweight and efficient frequency-domain multilayer perceptron (FDMLP) to capture cross-feature dependencies; combined with LSTM, it enables joint modeling across feature and temporal dimensions.
Jia, Y. B., Su, X. L., Singh, V. P., Zhao, B. N., Zhang, T., Chu, J. D., & Wu, H. J. (In revision, 2nd round). A Novel Hybrid Predictive Model Based on Mixture Density Networks with a Weighted Conformal Inference Strategy for Runoff Interval Prediction Across Australia. Water Resources Research.
Affiliations: Northwest A&F University (NWAFU); Texas A&M University (TAMU); China Three Gorges University (CTGU).
Jia, Y. B., Su, X. L., Wu, H. J., Yan, H. W., & Zhu, X. Y. (In press). Enhancing Streamflow Prediction Using Cutting-edge Deep Learning Models and Seasonal-Trend Decomposition. Water Resources Management.
Affiliations: Northwest A&F University (NWAFU). Contribution: Three emerging AI-based time-series models (FITS, FGN, PatchTST) were pioneered in runoff prediction and systematically evaluated in conjunction with four seasonal-trend decomposition (STD) methods, providing new insights for optimizing model-preprocessing synergy.
